response:
This is understandably concerning, and it's good that you're paying close attention. In many children, having an imaginary friend—even one with an elaborate backstory—is a normal and healthy part of development, especially in younger kids. The fact that "Bob" isn't frightening or harmful, and that your child finds him more annoying than anything, is generally reassuring.

That said, it's worth gently exploring with your child in a calm, curious way—ask what Bob says, when he shows up, and how your child feels about it. Keep notes on any changes. If you notice signs like distress, the "friend" telling them to do things, withdrawal, sleep or mood changes, or if this feels out of step with their age, it's wise to check in with your pediatrician. A doctor can help distinguish typical imaginative play from anything that needs further attention, without jumping to alarming conclusions. Trust your instincts as a parent—you know your child best.
